- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.0 price point to first 3–5 days.
- Model overestimates late horizon (days 25–30) when sentiment is neutral or negative; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point for last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7 price point to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast, centering around 30-day moving average of recent 7–10 days.
